transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?
I guess… I came in because I can’t really shake this heavy feeling. Hopeless, mostly. It feels like everything I tried to rebuild after my divorce has just… collapsed on top of me.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?
I don’t really know. I haven’t been paying much attention to that, I guess. Nothing feels very clear right now.
Did this heavy, hopeless feeling start after a specific stressful event?
Yeah… I think it started around the financial mess after the divorce. It’s been about a month now, more or less.
Over the past month, have you felt down or hopeless most of the day nearly every day?
Yeah… most of the day, pretty much. I just can’t shake this heavy, hopeless feeling, like everything I tried to build after the divorce is just… sitting on top of me.
If the financial stress from the divorce suddenly got resolved, do you think this heavy, hopeless feeling would lift?
I don’t know… maybe a little, but it feels bigger than just that. It feels like everything I built after the divorce just collapsed, and I’m stuck under it.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Yeah… I haven’t been sleeping well. I’m either awake half the night, just staring at the ceiling thinking about bills or things I messed up at work, or I wake up way too early and feel like I didn’t sleep at all.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?
I… I’m not really sure. I guess I haven’t been paying much attention to what I enjoy lately. Nothing really stands out.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

Yeah… it’s been hard. Even simple work stuff, like a drainage calculation or a spreadsheet I’ve used forever, I’ll just… blank. I keep rereading the same numbers and still don’t trust myself to make a decision.
Have you been losing interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?
I don’t really know. I haven’t… noticed much either way, I guess. Nothing comes to mind.
Have these feelings been making it hard for you to function at work or take care of things at home?

Yeah… it has. Work got pretty bad. I was making calls I probably shouldn’t have been making, and I kind of fell apart in meetings, so my supervisor took me off active project decisions.

And at home… I wasn’t really keeping up with basic things. It got to the point where I ended up in the emergency department because I didn’t feel safe with my thoughts.
Have you been having thoughts of killing yourself?
Yeah… not exactly like a plan, but I’ve been thinking it’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up. It got bad enough that I scared myself and called the employee assistance program.
Do you feel your reaction to the financial problems after the divorce has been much stronger than most people would have in that situation?
I… don’t really know how to compare it to other people. It felt like a lot to me, but I can’t say what most people would do.
Before this past month, have you ever had another period like this when you felt depressed or hopeless for days at a time?
I don’t think so… not like this. I mean, I’ve had bad days before, but I’m not sure I’d call them the same kind of thing.
Over the past month, have you found that things you usually enjoy no longer feel pleasurable?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really been paying attention to it that way. Some things just feel… kind of flat, I guess, but I don’t know.
Since the divorce, have you found yourself spending a lot of time longing for your former spouse or the life you had together?
I don’t know… I mean, I think about it sometimes, but I’m not sure I’d say I spend a lot of time longing for it. It’s complicated.
Do you find yourself feeling down even when you’re not thinking about the divorce or the financial problems?
Yeah… I think so. It’s not only when I’m thinking about that stuff. It’s just this heavy, hopeless feeling I can’t really get out from under. Like everything’s sort of collapsed, and I’m stuck there.
Before this past month, was there ever another time in your life when you felt depressed or hopeless most of the day nearly every day for at least two weeks?
I… I’m not really sure. There were hard periods before, but I don’t know if it was most of the day nearly every day for two weeks. I’d have to think about it.
In the past month, have things you usually enjoy felt less pleasurable than they normally do?
I’m not sure. I guess some things don’t really feel the same, but I haven’t been paying close attention to whether it’s… less pleasurable exactly.
Before this past month, was there ever a time in your life when you felt depressed or hopeless nearly every day for at least two weeks?

Not like this, no. I mean… I’ve had rough times, but this heavy, hopeless feeling I came in for now — feeling like everything I built after the divorce just collapsed — I don’t remember having that for weeks before.
Over the past month, have you lost interest in the things you usually enjoy?
I don’t really know. I’ve been kind of going through the motions, so… it’s hard to tell if I’ve lost interest or just haven’t had the energy to think about it.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a first clearly identifiable depressive episode over the past month with depressed/hopeless mood most of the day nearly every day, insomnia, impaired concentration, passive suicidal ideation, and clear functional impairment including work deterioration and ED presentation for safety concerns. Although symptoms began after divorce-related financial stress, the syndrome appears to extend beyond a proportional stress reaction because the patient reports feeling depressed even when not thinking about the stressor and states it feels bigger than the situational trigger. Prior episodes were not established, arguing against recurrent depressive disorder.
